headline: Cross-platform and timing-aware validation reshapes biomedical prediction claims
label: Validation Design In Biomedical Prediction
summary: Reported biomedical prediction performance depends on validation design, with cross-platform tests exposing drops that same-modality evaluation hides.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that evaluation design shapes claimed performance in biomedical machine learning. PRTS tests in-context prediction of clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes evaluation across 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets and 23 models, reporting that foundation models lead the comparison. Cross-modal anchoring corrects batch effects in one assay using a stable paired omic layer, without covariates, and outperforms ComBat on TCGA. Elflow pairs automated quality control with VICReg-based self-supervised representations for high-dimensional cytometry, benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. What is new is the pairing of standardized, cross-dataset or cross-platform benchmarking with method claims, rather than validation within a single cohort.
